solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Austrian showed the sky's the limit in this Olympic event

definitions.text: Austrian showed the sky's the limit in this Olympic event

parts.words: Austrian showed the sky's the limit in this Olympic event
parts.note: in 2012 the Austrian Felix Baumgartner leapt from a balloon at the edge of space, a leap from a very lofty start; the clue presents that stunt as an athletics field event

explanation.surface: A tribute to an Austrian daredevil whose record-breaking leap made the sky itself the only limit.
explanation.walkthrough: Baumgartner's 2012 skydive from the stratosphere was the loftiest leap ever made, which the clue files under an athletics discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic athletics event where competitors clear a raised bar is the clue's target; the Austrian's stunt was a leap from great altitude.

clue.text: They'll get in a stew if head of Synod supports the female bishop

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of Synod

explanation.surface: Church politics: a vote at Synod on women bishops gets people worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley, thyme and the like are flavourings added to a casserole.

clue.text: Queue to join section of road primarily intended for first among athletes

indicators.note: for signals one letter standing in place of another

parts.note: to get in lane is to move into a section of the road

indicators.note: first among points to the opening letter of athletes
primarily points to the opening letter of intended

explanation.surface: Instructions to athletes heading for the Olympic Park to take the special lane.
explanation.walkthrough: In GET IN LANE, the first letter of 'intended' replaces the first letter of 'athletes', A becoming I.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait one's turn in a line of people is to form a queue.

clue.text: Hall and toilets for emergency fuel containers

parts.note: Jerry Hall is the American model
cans is US slang for toilets

explanation.surface: A list of supplies: a hall, toilets and spare fuel cans.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-sided metal cans for carrying petrol, first used by German forces, are reserve fuel carriers.

clue.text: Docking point from runner taking gold, silver and bronze finally

parts.note: Mo Farah, the British distance runner who won double gold in 2012
or is gold in heraldry
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of bronze

explanation.surface: A runner collecting a full set of Olympic medals.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where a boat is tied up or anchored is a berth for vessels.

clue.text: Badger shot with kit that's old‑fashioned

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so the letters of badger are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A badger is shot by someone wearing antique hunting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for clothed or dressed, i.e. wearing one's kit, in a dated literary register.

clue.text: President isolated by defection of more than half of diplomats externally?

indicators.text: defection of more than half of
indicators.note: defection of more than half means six of the eleven letters leave
externally says the letters that go are from the outside of the word

parts.note: ambassadors are senior diplomats

explanation.surface: Syria's president is left isolated as diplomats defect.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AMB and ORS, six of eleven letters, from the outside of AMBASSADORS leaves the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashar al-Assad is the Syrian head of state.

clue.text: Suffering financially, rail company rejected knockout with energy

parts.note: BR was British Rail

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation is turned back

parts.note: KO is a knockout in boxing
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rail firm in money trouble turns down a knockout bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being penniless or bankrupt is to be in financial distress.

clue.text: Out of favour, Director-General was quick to accept income support

indicators.note: to accept means the abbreviation takes another inside

parts.note: IS is short for Income Support, a UK benefit
raced means went fast

explanation.surface: The BBC's Director-General quit in 2012 amid scandal, having hurried to take his pay-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has fallen into shame or lost standing is in disrepute.

clue.text: Tit for tat violence ending after punishment taken up by Football Association

indicators.note: taken by means held inside the abbreviation

parts.note: FA is the Football Association

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the pieces read upwards
after means the following letter comes later

parts.note: the rod is a symbol of punishment

indicators.note: ending points to the last letter of violence

explanation.surface: Sounds like a football disciplinary report on retaliation after a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Tit for tat is rhyming slang for hat, shortened to titfer. ROD then E, read 'up', gives EDOR, 'taken' in by FA.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt brimmed hat is the headwear meant by the rhyming slang.

clue.text: Source of spin — rubbish, alternatively

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about political spin: it is all rubbish, or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter's or turbine's revolving blade assembly is what makes it spin.

clue.text: Right away, Curiosity digs around bottom of Mars — but such leg protection there's optimistic!

indicators.note: around tells us the two pieces wrap round a letter
away tells us the letter for right is removed from the vehicle's name

parts.note: Curiosity is the NASA Mars rover
hoes means digs with a hoe

indicators.note: bottom of points to the final letter of the planet's name

explanation.surface: As NASA's Curiosity rover digs on Mars, protective footwear for its legs would be wildly optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' removes R from ROVER to leave OVER; with HOES (digs) this goes 'around' S, the last letter of Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber covers worn over shoes to keep the feet and lower legs dry are a kind of protective footwear.

clue.text: New York's tip caught by unfortunate storm

indicators.note: caught by means the letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: sad can mean unfortunate or regrettable

indicators.note: tip points to the first letter of York

explanation.surface: New York's southern tip was hit by a disastrous storm, as happened in October 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurricane Sandy was the named storm that struck the New York coast in 2012.

clue.text: A grand old celebration turns to affirmation — Queen's annus mirabilis?

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: turns means the word for the party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
yea is an old word of assent, yes
R is short for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A grand old jubilee party ends in a resounding yes: the Queen's marvellous year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses DO to OD. 'Queen's' gives R, for Regina; the 's is part of the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Annus mirabilis is Latin for a wonderful twelve months, the opposite of the Queen's famous annus horribilis.

clue.text: Pasty attracting tax after rule is brought in behind closed doors

indicators.note: brought in means the letter for rule is inserted
attracting means the pie draws the tax inside it

parts.note: a pasty is a kind of pie
VAT is value added tax
R is the abbreviation for rule, as in R for rex or regulation

explanation.surface: A reference to the 2012 'pasty tax' row, when VAT on hot pasties was brought in by a rule change agreed in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting' puts VAT inside PIE (PIVATE), then 'brought in' inserts R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in secret or away from the public is done confidentially, out of public view.

clue.text: Extremely like a policeman, according to Chief Whip? Drop left most stony-faced?

indicators.note: drop means the letter is moved down in a down entry

parts.words: Extremely like a policeman, according to Chief Whip
parts.note: in 2012 the Chief Whip Andrew Mitchell allegedly called police officers plebs, so most pleb-like

explanation.surface: Mocks the 2012 'Plebgate' row: the Chief Whip should drop his stony expression and leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving L lower in the word changes PLEB to PEBBL.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn with many small stones, the superlative of pebbly; stony is the link.

clue.text: Harm CIA with flapping tongue

indicators.note: flapping suggests wild movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Loose talk could harm the CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The official language of Ethiopia; tongue is a common synonym for language.

clue.text: Grant-aided body cut back

definitions.meaning: the press-reform campaign backed by actor Hugh Grant after the phone-hacking scandal

explanation.surface: A funded organisation suffers spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaign group name doubles as the past tense of chopping something away; Hugh Grant's support explains 'Grant-aided'.

clue.text: Softening, extended credit again in Government

parts.note: to re-lend is to lend again; lent is its past

explanation.surface: The Government softens its stance and extends credit again.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming less severe or giving way is yielding.

clue.text: Head of Bank inferior? Balls approved

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of Bank

parts.note: less can mean of lower rank or inferior
Ed Balls was the Labour shadow chancellor in 2012

explanation.surface: A jibe at the Governor of the Bank of England as inferior, with Labour's Ed Balls nodding approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given a blessing has been sanctioned or endorsed.

clue.text: E.g. Facebook stock regularly ignored in catastrophe

indicators.note: in means the picked letters are placed inside

parts.note: doom means ruin or catastrophe

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter of stock is dropped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: Facebook's 2012 stock flotation was a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet-based company, a typical example being a social network.

clue.text: Duck! End of bell having flown off disastrously and caused damage

indicators.note: disastrously suggests a mess, so the letters are scrambled
having flown off means a letter is removed from bell
end of points to the last letter of bell

explanation.surface: A warning shout as a bell's clapper flies off and does damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of bell having flown off' leaves BEL; with DUCK it is rearranged 'disastrously'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bent or crumpled something under stress is to have damaged it.

clue.text: Zanzibar is tax haven for hot drinks vendor, perhaps

indicators.note: a haven shelters something, here a word sheltered within the phrase

explanation.surface: Zanzibar is a tax haven for a coffee seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee-bar server who makes espresso drinks; 'perhaps' because other vendors exist.

clue.text: Freer rate fixed within inter‑bank lending one

indicators.note: within means the rearranged letters go inside

parts.note: LIBOR is the London Inter-Bank Offered Rate, a lending rate between banks

indicators.note: fixed, as in rigged, signals an anagram of rate

explanation.surface: The 2012 LIBOR scandal: an inter-bank lending rate was rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' turns RATE into ERAT, placed 'within' LIBOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets people free from captivity or oppression is a deliverer or emancipator.

clue.text: Stunt artist's cry of distress, hanging around middle of wire upside down

indicators.note: upside down in a down entry means read from bottom to top
hanging around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a sob is a cry of distress

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letters of wire

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson, stuck on a zip wire in 2012, cries out while dangling upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: SOB 'hanging around' IR gives SIROB, read 'upside down'.
explanation.definitionFit: London mayor Boris Johnson performed a zip-wire stunt in 2012 and got stuck, a stunt performer of sorts.

clue.text: Olympic bigwig turning up to urge gold

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An Olympic chief turns up to urge athletes on to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Rogge was president of the International Olympic Committee in 2012.

clue.text: Medal-winner missing start of Murray's game

indicators.note: missing start of means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Andy Murray plays tennis

explanation.surface: An Olympic medallist misses the start of Andy Murray's match.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica Ennis won heptathlon gold for Britain at the 2012 London Olympics.

clue.text: See rowing team change direction

indicators.note: change direction means one compass point, east, gives way to another, south

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Watch the rowing crew turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision, or a view, is what one sees.

clue.text: Outrageous, English, say, taking on Greek debts …

indicators.note: taking on means the example abbreviation takes in the Greek code

parts.note: English is an example of a language; e.g. means for example
GRE is the Olympic and international code for Greece
IOUs are debts, from I owe you

explanation.surface: An English commentator finds it outrageous to take on the Greek debt burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking on' puts GRE inside EG. The ellipsis links this clue to the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shockingly bad or flagrant conduct is described as outrageous.

clue.text: … having unknown amount lost in deficit

indicators.note: lost means the letter is removed

parts.note: having can mean possessing, owning
n is the algebraic symbol for an unknown number

explanation.surface: Continuing the Greek story: the nation, with an unknown sum gone missing, is in deficit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in arrears or in debt is to be still due to pay money.

clue.text: Swing states providing samples

indicators.note: swing suggests movement, so the letters of states are rearranged

explanation.surface: In the 2012 US election, the swing states give a sample of national opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Small portions tried to judge flavour are tasters or samples.

clue.text: Pussy Riot dispute getting vicious

parts.note: pussy is a pet word for a cat
a riot is a violent disturbance or fight

explanation.surface: The Russian protest band Pussy Riot's quarrel with the authorities turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiteful, scratching quarrel, typically between women, is the idiomatic term.
